summary.en: Pakistan condemned a Houthi strike on the Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh and demanded an end to all Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, while a separate Houthi attempt on the same facility was also thwarted. In northwest Pakistan a police officer was killed in a terror attack, and a Pakistani military drone strike in Balochistan’s Kachhi district killed five fighters including a commander. Punjab officials linked regional smog to cross-border Diwali fireworks from India, prompting an LPG strike call to be withdrawn and later postponed after talks. The conflict still accounts for 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistan fordømte et houthi-angrep på Saudi Aramco-bygningen i Riyadh og krevde en slutt på alle houthi-angrep mot Saudi-Arabia, mens et separat houthi-forsøk på samme anlegg også ble avverget. I nordvestlige Pakistan ble en politimann drept i et terrorangrep, og et pakistansk militært dronered i Kachhi-distriktet i Balochistan drepte fem krigere, inkludert en kommandør. Punjab-myndighetene knyttet regional smog til grenseoverskridende Diwali-fyrverkeri fra India, noe som førte til at en LPG-streik ble trukket tilbake og senere utsatt etter samtaler. Konflikten står fortsatt for 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
